codelines.evidence: src/fares.ts contains the fare logic. fareFor (line 8) checks `if (rider.age > 65) return CONCESSION_FARE_CENTS` on line 10 — the boundary is strictly greater-than, so a rider aged exactly 65 falls through to BASE_FARE_CENTS (350) instead of the concession fare (175). This is MOCK3-1. Tests in test/fares.test.ts cover ages 30, 8, and 70 but do not test age 65, so the boundary gap is uncaught. No schedule or departure-board symbols were found in this codeline.

src/schedule.ts contains the departure-board logic. formatStops (line 4) loops `for (let i = 0; i < stops.length - 1; i++)` on line 6, which iterates up to the second-to-last stop, omitting the final stop entirely. totalMinutes (line 12) correctly reads the last element's minutes, so the journey length is right while the rendered list is short. This is MOCK3-2. Tests in test/schedule.test.ts assert the arrow separator and the first stop name but never assert the last stop appears, so the omission is uncaught. No fare-related symbols were found in this codeline.

recommendedInvestigators.focus: Confirm the age-65 boundary condition in fareFor and review whether any other code paths or callers depend on the current `> 65` behaviour.
recommendedInvestigators.why: fareFor uses a strict greater-than comparison for the concession age boundary; the ticket says 65-and-over should qualify, and the test suite has no age-65 case to catch the discrepancy.

recommendedInvestigators.focus: Confirm the loop bound in formatStops and check whether any caller or display path compensates for the missing last stop.
recommendedInvestigators.why: formatStops iterates to `stops.length - 1`, dropping the final stop; the test suite only checks for the arrow separator and first stop name, never the last stop.
